newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar plunges, rates jump in response.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar plunges, rates jump in response.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar dived overnight to a 19-month low and traded lower during Friday, with traders citing pressure from U.S. hedge funds, prompting a sharp jump in 90-day bank bill rates from 7.7 percent to 8.6 percent.

The kiwi dollar slid more than one U.S. cent to below 0.6500 by 10.30 a.m. (2230 GMT) from a Thursday close of 0.6600, and dealers speculated the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (central bank) would have to comment during the session to ease the pain.
Dealers said the kiwi was being pummelled by hedge funds, and New Zealand was coming under the microscope after the ripple of action across South East Asian currencies.
The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index dropped about 100 basis points to 64.50, near its lowest level for 13 months.
"It's heavy, heavy, heavy," said a dealer, saying big selling out of New York had driven the kiwi down.
"Unless there is some fundamental change from the Reserve Bank you are going to be looking at 64 cents and you could see it this afternoon. There are just no buyers," he said.
